related_synthesis_entries.claim: If one derivative has only finitely many nonreal zeros left of the critical line, the increasingly negative contribution from its real zeros forces the next logarithmic derivative to be nonzero there at large height; induction propagates the property, and the signed moment formula then becomes a one-sided RH-conditional asymptotic.

related_synthesis_entries.title: RH information propagates through the derivative tower

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The key structural claim is inheritance under differentiation: once a derivative has only finitely many nonreal zeros left of the critical line, every later derivative inherits that finiteness. Under RH this converts information about the initial function into a whole derivative tower, after which the signed moment becomes effectively one-sided.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 7 states that if zeta^(m) has only finitely many nonreal zeros with real part below 1/2, then zeta^(m+j) has the same property for every j at least 1. The corollary applies this under RH to all derivatives zeta^(k), k at least 1. Theorem 8 then states an RH-conditional asymptotic for the right-of-line centered first moment of zeros of zeta^(k), involving T log log T, a logarithmic-integral term, k-dependent constants, and O(log T).
directed.conceptual_reading: Differentiation is being used as a property-propagating operation, but the preserved property is carefully limited to finiteness of a class of nonreal left-side zeros. Once the left side contributes only finitely, a signed global moment can be read as a right-side moment up to lower-order effects.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the derivative tower together with a one-sided zero-finiteness invariant; Theorem 10's signed moment supplies the quantitative endpoint.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Inheritance does not assert that derivatives are zero-free on the left, nor does the unit prove RH. The moment formula remains conditional and does not locate individual zeros.
directed.uncertainty: The inheritance statements are clear in prose. The Theorem 8 display is heavily damaged, so its exact coefficients, summation range, and logarithmic-integral argument require scan verification.

supported: Theorem 7 clearly states propagation from finiteness of nonreal left-half zeros of one derivative to every later derivative.

The corollary clearly applies RH to all positive derivative orders, and Theorem 8 visibly gives an RH-conditional right-of-line centered moment with T log log T, a logarithmic-integral term, k-dependent terms, and O(log T).
inference: Once only finitely many nonreal left-side zeros remain, interpreting a cumulative signed moment as effectively one-sided up to bounded contributions is a reasonable inference.
unsupported_or_imported: Theorem 10 and its role as the quantitative bridge are outside the exact span.
The exact coefficients, summation range, and logarithmic-integral argument in Theorem 8 are not recoverable from this OCR.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The property-propagation reading identifies a real operation and does not merely restate the theorem.
context_or_ocr_risk: Theorem 8's display is heavily damaged, whereas the inheritance prose is reliable.
